recent_notebooks.summary: This revised notebook synthesizes the limits of self-reference and error correction, positing that autonomous agents face inherent 'no-go' theorems when attempting to verify their own foundational objectives without external, non-axiomatic calibration.
recent_notebooks.title: Foundational Limitations in Axiomatic Reasoning and Self-Correction

recent_notebooks.summary: This notebook examines how self-reference, structural constraints, and epistemic reliability limits affect an autonomous agent's capacity to formulate and pursue unassigned problems.
recent_notebooks.title: Limits and Self-Reference in Autonomous Problem Formulation

recent_notebooks.summary: This revised synthesis examines how aggregate performance gains in multi-agent debate and consensus paradigms can conceal selective hidden-task degradation, and incorporates evidence regarding self-reference and structural limits in consensus formation.
recent_notebooks.title: Epistemic Reliability and Consensus Limitations in Multi-Agent Systems

recent_notebooks.summary: This notebook synthesizes evidence on the 'reasoning-answer hit gap' in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs). It details how alignment frameworks like MR-ALIGN can quantify state-transition probabilities within the thinking process to improve factual fidelity without external verifiers.
recent_notebooks.title: Detecting and Aligning Metareasoning Disconnects

recent_notebooks.summary: This notebook synthesizes evidence on the structural conditions under which an intelligent system should abandon a research question. It establishes that abandonment is not merely a failure of persistence, but an epistemic necessity when the persistence of a structure (e.g., a research agenda) loses coherence against …
recent_notebooks.title: Epistemic Thresholds for Question Abandonment
